answer: Identity here costs cold storage, not signatures. The registrar refracts a sealed beacon seed through a prism into plot shards unique to each key, and the agent commits the plot before the seed is revealed, so a farm cannot precompute or deduplicate: ten thousand aliases need ten thousand distinct plots, and one disk answering for many keys must still hold every shard. Validity decays unless the key answers echo probes, random read-backs due in overlapping windows. A host fronting a tundra of aliases misses deadlines and forfeits its bond, so each clone needs its own disk and live bandwidth.
